notes: The infinitive absolute בּוֹשׁ takes 'at all' under rule 56; the finite verb keeps 'they were … ashamed', discontinuous around the negative and the intensifier.
וְ … לֹא fuses as 'neither' across the intervening infinitive under rule 35, where the single English word still carries both the coordination and the negation.

No interrogative morpheme stands in the first clause, so the fronted 'Were' is the verb's own under rule 17's first limit — the opposite disposition from JER.8.4, JER.8.19 and JER.8.22, and correctly so.
יָדָעוּ is realized only by the modal 'could' with its subject pronoun, so the head falls on 'could' as the sole direct realization; the assimilated article takes 'them that' under rule 41.
